title: The Dungeon Dive's 2020 Retrospective and Look Forward to 2021!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B5xTJMahaK4

No awards show this year — Daniel (@dungeondive) says he simply didn't play enough new games to make one meaningful. Of 130 videos, only about 20 covered 2020 releases. What replaces it is the year's most direct statement of what the channel is for.

The Patreon launched (40 patrons, well past his expectation of 10 or 20), the first top-ten lists ran, and the *Art Of* series began — covering Cave Evil and Talisman 2nd edition, scored with his own music. He commits to more of it, on the grounds that celebrating game artists is the thing that distinguishes him from other board game channels.

The thesis arrives via the Sword & Sorcery Saga project: reading the old fiction has convinced him that sword and sorcery is effectively dead as a modern publishing genre and has migrated into board and video games. That makes the book coverage inseparable from the game coverage — even though, he notes, the book videos get the fewest views and the most downvotes, and he'll keep making them anyway.

Disappointments are candid: Secrets of the Lost Station, D6, Medara sold without a review to avoid dogpiling a Kickstarter darling. Highlights are books — first-printing DAW Elric paperbacks with Whelan covers, and a 17-pound Taschen fantasy art volume.

----

If the audience for a creator's favourite work is the smallest, should they keep making it?
